scope_plain: Most of Maury County, including all of Mount Pleasant and the north and west side of Columbia, under the U.S. House map Tennessee redrew in May 2026. The new 5th runs from Maury and Williamson counties west across rural West Tennessee into part of Memphis.
office_explainer: One of 435 House members. Writes federal laws and votes on the budget and taxes. Two-year term.
why_it_matters: Open seat: Rep. Andy Ogles lost the August Republican primary to Charlie Hatcher. The lines are new too: the May 2026 redraw moved about 19,662 Maury County addresses from one U.S. House district to another, per the Election Commission.

candidates.name: Charlie Hatcher
candidates.background: Former Tennessee agriculture commissioner and a dairy farmer, per NewsChannel 5. Republican nominee from College Grove, per the Secretary of State's candidate list.

own_words.text: The number one priority would be cost of living.
Tariffs are a tool; they can be used effectively, sometimes badly.

candidates.name: Chaz Molder
candidates.background: Mayor of Columbia since 2018, re-elected in 2022, per the Tennessee Democratic Party; he isn't running for mayor again. Democratic nominee from Columbia, per the Secretary of State's candidate list.

own_words.text: What I want to get to work immediately on is working to reduce the cost of living.
And constituent services has got to be the number one priority.

candidates.name: James A. Johnson
candidates.background: Independent candidate from Memphis, per the Secretary of State's candidate list.

where: NewsChannel 5's Oct 21 forum report (he did not take part)

candidates.name: Micheál (Me-Haul) O'Leary
candidates.background: Irish-born businessman and former local elected official in California, per NewsChannel 5. Independent candidate from Nashville, per the Secretary of State's candidate list.

own_words.text: As an independent, I will have that independent voice.
I’m running to represent you. You are going to be grading my report card.

scope_plain: Part of Maury County, including downtown Columbia and much of the city's south and east side, under the U.S. House map Tennessee redrew in May 2026. The new 9th runs about 200 miles, from part of Memphis east across rural Tennessee to parts of Maury, Williamson and Rutherford counties.
office_explainer: One of 435 House members. Writes federal laws and votes on the budget and taxes. Two-year term.
why_it_matters: Open seat: Rep. Steve Cohen of Memphis isn't running again after the May 2026 redraw split his district, per Roll Call. The 9th, long a Memphis district, now reaches Columbia.

candidates.name: Brent Taylor
candidates.background: State senator from outside Memphis who owns a funeral home business, per NewsChannel 5; a former Memphis City Council member, per WSMV. Republican nominee from Eads, per the Secretary of State's candidate list.

own_words.text: What I want to do is, I want to continue doing what I have been doing in the state senate. And that is cutting wasteful spending. We have to bring wasteful Washington spending under control. I also want to unleash American energy.
Look the voters already know the choice here. The choice is competence or chaos. We don't need a debate to prove that.

candidates.name: Justin J. Pearson
candidates.background: State representative for a Memphis district (House District 86), per the Tennessee Democratic Party. Democratic nominee from Memphis, per the Secretary of State's candidate list.

own_words.text: The first thing we need to do is end this endless war in Iran. It was done illegally in the first place, but that has increased gas prices for consumers substantially.
I want to debate Brent Taylor anytime, anyplace, anywhere because the voters deserve to hear the very different visions for the state that we have.

where: NewsChannel 5 and WSMV coverage of the race

candidates.name: Michelle Davis Head
candidates.background: Independent candidate from Lewisburg, per the Secretary of State's candidate list.

where: NewsChannel 5 and WSMV coverage of the race

scope_plain: Only voters who live inside Columbia city limits; the whole city votes. If you live outside city limits (even with a Columbia mailing address), the city's races aren't on your ballot.
office_explainer: Chairs and votes on the seven-member city council, speaks for the city to other governments, and names people to city boards with the council's approval. A city manager hired by the council runs the city day to day. Nonpartisan, four-year term.
why_it_matters: Open seat: Mayor Chaz Molder isn't running again. He is on this ballot as the Democratic nominee for the U.S. House.

candidates.name: Timothy Johnson
candidates.background: Pastor of a local church, per Main Street Maury's report on the Sept 22 mayoral forum.

own_words.text: "We may be doing too much, and we may need to slow down a little bit."
"We need to expand our tax base strategically."
own_words.source_label: Main Street Maury, Oct 18 NAACP forum

candidates.name: Jai Lipscomb
candidates.background: Realtor who runs the nonprofit All Hands on Deck, per Main Street Maury's report on the Sept 22 mayoral forum. The county's petition list names her Jolita Lipscomb.

own_words.text: "Growth is not the enemy, irresponsible growth is the enemy."
"I think we need to… diversify the homes that we’re building."

candidates.name: Stewart Parker
candidates.background: Businessman and chair of the county's Industrial Development Board, per Main Street Maury's report on the Sept 22 mayoral forum.

own_words.text: "If we want to make sure our infrastructure is keeping up… and we’re not paying for it ourselves, we need to improve our relationship with the state."
"Have we made it so difficult that a local builder cannot build a reasonably priced house here, or… buy an existing home and not increase the price because… of the restrictions within the city?"

candidates.name: Eric Previti
candidates.background: Maury County commissioner for District 2 for 12 years, through August 2026, per Main Street Maury.

own_words.text: "Where are the new stores to support these neighborhoods, complexes and apartments? I think we need to work on that infrastructure."
"The city of Columbia needs to formally recognize that there’s a homeless problem."

candidates.name: Ashley Townsend
candidates.background: Legal assistant with Barnes Law, per Main Street Maury's report on the Sept 22 mayoral forum.

own_words.text: "If we don’t have the roads in place… the proper water and sewer systems… [and] emergency response teams, then we do need, most certainly, a moratorium or something to that effect on our residential development."
"I want individuals to be empowered… not placated… [or] pushed out."
own_words.source_label: Main Street Maury, Oct 18 NAACP forum

scope_plain: Only voters who live inside Mount Pleasant city limits; the whole city votes. Pick up to two of the three candidates. If you live outside city limits (even with a Mount Pleasant mailing address), this race isn't on your ballot.
office_explainer: One of five commissioners who govern the city: they pass city laws, hire the city manager and choose one of themselves as mayor. Four-year term.
why_it_matters: None of the three candidates sits on the commission now, per the city's list of commissioners, so both places go to someone new.
